coverage.statement: Explain the purpose, characteristics, and typical use cases of the HTTP GET method, including how parameters are passed.
Explain the purpose, characteristics, and typical use cases of the HTTP POST method, including how payload data is transmitted.
Distinguish between GET and POST methods based on data visibility, caching, idempotency, and intended side effects.
Explain the general meaning of HTTP status code series: 2xx (Success), 4xx (Client Error), and 5xx (Server Error).
Distinguish whether a given scenario or status code reflects a successful operation (2xx), a client-side issue (4xx), or an internal server failure (5xx).

rubric.rationale: All objectives (O1-O5) are fully covered in the text and directly assessed through the knowledge checks and scenario exercises.
Key terms like idempotent, payload, and status code families are clearly defined on first use with plain English explanations.
The lesson moves logically from a motivating hook about password leaks into GET/POST mechanics, status codes, tracing examples, and practice.
Concrete HTTP message traces and real-world scenarios provide excellent application opportunities with clear self-check solutions.
The self-paced design includes frequent prompts to write down answers and check solutions, keeping the learner actively engaged.
The technical depth and terminology are perfectly calibrated for first- or second-year engineering students.

strengths: Engaging hook that immediately connects HTTP security and status codes to a realistic developer bug.
Clear distinction between data hiding (POST body) and data encryption (TLS/HTTPS).
Well-structured HTTP request and response trace examples that demystify raw protocol syntax.
Comprehensive self-check scenarios that require learners to classify both methods and error categories.
